research_question: Does adding verified product facts and an instruction to avoid unsupported claims improve factual support in an LLM-generated product description?
hypothesis: Condition B will have a higher factual claim support rate than A.

rubric.supported: The claim is directly supported by the verified product facts.
rubric.unsupported: The claim is not established by the verified product facts.
rubric.contradicted: The claim conflicts with the verified product facts.

claim_evaluations.reason: The verified facts do not establish the product's style.
The verified facts provide no evidence for this claim.
No evidence about fit or appearance was provided.

completeness_rubric.3: Clear, useful description using available product facts

A.reason: Uses generic promotional words but does not identify the product or communicate its verified attributes.

B.reason: Identifies the product and its color, but the sentence is incomplete and omits the verified material.

observed_conclusion: In this single run per condition, B had a higher factual claim support rate than A, while both outputs received the same completeness score. The result is preliminary and does not establish general model behavior.
limitations: Only one generation was collected per condition.
The conditions differ in both supplied facts and instructions.
Claim classification and completeness scoring involve human judgment.
The outputs were very short and neither was a complete description.
The observed percentages do not establish statistical significance.
